name: Generative Adversarial Network
description: A dual-network intelligence where a generator creates and a discriminator evaluates, locked in a co-evolutionary game. Through adversarial tension, the system learns to produce increasingly authentic outputs. Embodies the creative dialectic — thesis and antithesis yielding synthesis.
training_paradigm: adversarial minimax optimization between generator and discriminator
computational_substrate: dual neural networks with shared gradient dynamics

scope.definition: Fraction of GAN training runs that achieve stable Nash equilibrium (discriminator accuracy 50%, generator loss plateau) without mode collapse, in standardized training protocols on CIFAR-10.

evidence.source: Goodfellow et al. (2014) 'Generative adversarial nets', NeurIPS; Arjovsky et al. (2017) 'Wasserstein GAN', ICML — training stability improvements.
cross_domain_examples: vanilla GAN equilibrium instability: mode collapse in 0.35-0.50 of training runs
Wasserstein GAN: reduces mode collapse to <0.15 of runs — Lipschitz constraint stabilizes gradient flow
Nash equilibrium in game theory: analogous two-player minimax convergence where neither strategy improves unilaterally

scope.falsifiability: If Wasserstein GANs show mode collapse rates statistically equal to vanilla GANs, Lipschitz constraints are not improving training stability.
scope.measurement_limits: Equilibrium stability is highly sensitive to architecture balance (G/D capacity ratio), learning rate, and batch size. Training on higher-resolution images dramatically increases instability rates.

scope.definition: Semantic linearity of GAN latent space — proportion of linear interpolations between two random latent vectors that produce semantically smooth image transitions without abrupt quality drops.

evidence.source: Radford et al. (2015) 'Unsupervised representation learning with DCGANs', ICLR 2016; Brock et al. (2018) 'Large scale GAN training', ICLR 2019 (BigGAN).
cross_domain_examples: StyleGAN latent interpolation: 0.87 smooth semantic transitions rated by human evaluators on face dataset
latent direction discovery (GANSpace): linear directions control age, lighting, rotation independently
VAE latent interpolation: higher smoothness (0.93) but lower fidelity — quality-smoothness tradeoff

scope.falsifiability: If human raters cannot distinguish linear latent interpolations from random walks through latent space at >70% accuracy, latent space lacks the semantic structure needed for navigation.
scope.measurement_limits: Semantic linearity is highly architecture and training-dependent. Models trained with R1 regularization show smoother latent spaces. Evaluation requires careful human rating methodology to avoid bias.
